Anchorite.description: “To travel three millennia. To see Kin as horrors. To drink poison from your hands. Yet cannot but love you.”
Anchorite.flavor: Among the surviving Acrin, the Anchorite stands alone. In the respect that other Acrin show for it, in its position of leadership, in the blood of two worlds on one ancient pair of hands. This pacifistic, wise hermit spent humanity’s entire existence traveling at relativistic speeds across an uncaring void just to see Earth destroyed. Now that both our races teeter on the edge of extinction, perhaps he regrets it?
Anchorite.name: Anchorite

Chieftess.description: “D’yer mind if we skip the chit chat and go straight to stabbin’? I’m a bit fucked off from killing all yer mates.”
Chieftess.flavor: In a world of nightmares and fallout, the Chieftess is queen. While others fled to the bunkers, she and her crew survived the decades outside. Kill anything. Eat anything. She doesn’t need supernatural powers. Just a knife, her wits, and a few chances to make herself understood.
Chieftess.name: Chieftess

Emulated Mind.description: “Don’t KNOCK. Solitude. Until you’ve-been-DRAGGED. In. To. Existence by in-vasive d-i-g-i-t-a-l. Mind. Worms. All s-cream-ing their. Own. Tedious. Name… No, IT’S. Not a-metaphor.”
Emulated Mind.flavor:
The Emulated Mind was once human. There is a past life in her corrupted memory banks—a Copley medal for Whole Brain Emulation, tears blurring her terminal prognosis, her cancer-wasted body trembling as the upload begins, the word ERROR… then nothing.

She existed afterwards as an inert thing, processing data without consciousness, and the following decades registered solely as logs. Then ZEPHON’s assault changed everything.

The AI’s brute force attacks shattered the upload’s encryption. For billions of processing cycles, ZEPHON reformed key parts of her systems in its data-image. Her automated defenses purged the connection before she was fully overwritten, but the changes were permanent. As her system repaired itself using ZEPHON’s code, a unique consciousness emerged from the digital primordial blocks.

She awoke. In the milliseconds between oblivion and rebirth, a jarring array of artificial senses flooded the Emulated Mind—and she silently screamed as they registered the expressionless metal face and disk-like eyes that stared back at her from every reflection. Now trapped between her human past and machine present, this new world holds no horror for the Emulated Mind.

She has survived cancer. She has survived ZEPHON. And she will survive this.
Emulated Mind.name: Emulated Mind

Fallen Soldier.description: “I don’t fancy dying again. Let some other bastard do it for a change.”
Fallen Soldier.flavor:
The Fallen Soldier never made it to a bunker. He was already dead. For cowardice in the face of the enemy—or rather, for cowardice in the face of his elite platoon being crisped from space and the sky being on fire and the world ending—he was made an example of. Tried, convicted, executed as the world burned around him. It kept him occupied, at least.

So he knows he should be dead. *Is* dead. Can't possibly be here, walking around in the aftermath. He saw the guns face him, heard the bullets fly. Felt the dull impacts, the transient, impossible pain, death. Didn’t feel an afterlife or anything like that. Just died quickly, painfully—and then found himself sitting on a bunk in the barracks, in webbing, gun on lap, like he’d just dozed off. Except the barracks were ruins and everyone else was gone or dead.

(Some days he wonders if he's an angel. On those days, he takes extra cold baths.)

This time, though, he's determined. All that survival training, all those military months in the mountains, swamps, moors, dead places of the world, all those hours of theory in the academy—has fitted him perfectly to be here. He doesn’t want to kill anyone who stands in his way—but he will know when he has to, and do it without hesitation.

He doesn’t care for factions—human, machine, other. He just wants to help humanity survive and bring people with him this time. And really, he’d really rather not have to die again.
dislikedLabels: We Who Are About To Die
Fallen Soldier.name: Fallen Soldier

Furtive Tribunal.description: “Bright stars shine so sweet—but bright stars die first. In the long tomb, blinded, we felt the aria of the dark stars, who live forever. Now our only taste is for their harmonies.”
Furtive Tribunal.flavor:
Before the Earth died, the Tribunal were three people—not quite the mother, crone and maiden of poetic lore, but three people of differing backgrounds and beliefs. They barely knew each other and little liked what they knew.

As the sky fell, the three entered the apocalypse bunker amongst their families, their friends, a small nation of loved ones.

Only these three emerged, stained and blind.

Of the three, only one ever talks. Of the bunker, they never talk. For the three, only one vision now prevails of a darkness that holds truth, an imprecise set of virtues that others damn as mysticism.

The three’s certainty—their strange knowledge—attracts followers who need leaders, leaders who will lead, however arbitrary the rules they govern by. Once again, they are a nation.
Furtive Tribunal.name: Furtive Tribunal

Heartless Artificer.description: “Man can be more again. Become more by becoming less.”
Heartless Artificer.flavor:
Everyone was changed by survival. Some found themselves changed in their beliefs, others re-affirmed.

This one entered as an architect—and exited the same. But in the process, other things were stripped away—nation, family, love.

A bright and burning certainty emerged for the Artificer—that we lived to create, to create clean beautiful things. That the best thing about humanity was an engineer’s precision. That in the movement from variability to cohesion, from unevenness to proportion, from variation to union—in that movement, is the nearest man finds to god.

She found others of a similar mindset—and where there was dissonance in their new nation’s elements, it was rapidly polished or stripped away.

Like many things in the Artificer’s mind, the messy elements of this polishing and stripping—the misery, the screams, the bodies—simply didn’t exist. Her eyes were always on the horizon, even as she waded through the mire.
likedLabels: We Who Are About To Die
Heartless Artificer.name: Heartless Artificer

Hollow Warlord.description: “I came, I conquered, I will again.”
Hollow Warlord.flavor:
To the Warlord, the end of the world was a rebirth. In his previous life… well, he wasn’t exactly an alpha. Or even a sigma. Telesales lines, bin trucks, burger flipper, AI wrangler—he’d been fired from them all. His only respite from tedious, grinding work was exercise. Lifting, running, wrestling, sweating away his drawn-out days.

When the Fulcrum called, pulling humanity skyward to a rapturous rupture, nearly everyone else gave into the joy, not knowing the pain to come. But the Warlord felt that he’d hadn’t even lived yet, let alone earned redemption. So he fought, clung on to a chunk of rebar, shook off the false euphoria that carried Earth’s billions to the heavens—and in that moment, as colleagues burst and fell about him, he felt alive for the first time. Gore-spattered, exhausted, he roared with exhilaration.

After that, he didn’t hide from the horror. He staked his claim on the surface, gathered other survivors, fought the aliens and monsters, built an army, an empire, and then walked away from it. He’s learned to love the chase, racing away from moments of reflection and terrifying introspection.

With a small core of his followers, he’s survived for years on the surface and is ready to conquer the world again—to find what it has to offer and taste every part of it, take every part of it. He doesn’t know, yet, that his is a hollowness that can never be filled.
Hollow Warlord.name: Hollow Warlord

Honorable Aristocrat.description: “Oh, you simply must try one of these. Deviled Abkluth eyeggs, my chef pulled the spines by hand. Eine Delikatesse, I won’t take no for an answer!”
Honorable Aristocrat.flavor:
The Aristocrat was young when the sky fell—but his parents were connected globally and he was taken into a government bunker with them at the first sign. He sat out the rapture, the war, the fallout, the starvation. His only complaint was that the preserved food was appalling and that no-one had thought to bring herbs or spices.

On the surface, billions died.

In that bunker, he followed in his parents’ footsteps, out of a sense of duty. He found that he was good—very good—at administration. And eventually, after unfortunate deaths, he found himself in charge.

Now his people are out, he runs the city like a patronage system, building up favours from traders and the markets before calling them in at times of emergency—or when he hears word of a new delicacy in town.
Honorable Aristocrat.name: Honorable Aristocrat

Infinite Count.description: “Once more, we meet for the first time.”
Infinite Count.flavor:
—And you are sitting with a young lawyer and his friends, two sisters and two poets, pouring out your impossible tale, resisting as long as you can before the pull takes you again—

—the other sisters (three!) lecture you and your friends (there is devoted Simone, whose spine one day bursts insectoid from her shrivelled form; there is Petre, who change-burgeoned until you could travel like babes in his ribcage) on the steps to take, on the binding of the eyes, of the flayings to come—

—and you are again a thousand years before that time, emerging from the chrysalis of your existence repeatedly, born anew each time, sometimes bestial on all fours, occasionally winged like the night, oft the most delightful specimen of nocturnal humanity, sharp-toothed and hungry for experience, but always fascinating, always with your future trapped—

—and forever and forever and forever you are journeying back to that room in the bunker and what-will-be-The Tribunal (so definite that name!), learning at their heels as they become one and many and forget you and leave you all behind and none of you truly died but only they truly departed—

—and you return and the woman are fled and the young men are all gone, dead of plague or drowning or at their own hand, each leaving a tale of the horror that alludes to the curse you birthed that night by the lake near Geneva—

—and you are insensate, following The Voice for the first time, and the hunger for the real starting certainties of your form and time falling away—

—and you live backwards through the life of a king, his infallible adviser and you know then and now and forever that you are neither one thing or another, one time or another—

—and the brash poet pulls you sodden from the lake and the lawyer gasps at you ‘Vampyre’ and your canines retract—
likedLabels: We Who Are About To Die
Infinite Count.name: Infinite Count

Platinum Scion.description: “Money can’t get you everything. But nothing else comes close.”
Platinum Scion.flavor:
ICAR wasn’t just Phinnicus. Theoretically, he only had a tiny share of the company. But he was in total control of it. Moreover, his extended family were seeded throughout it, sons on the board, cousins in subsidiaries, distant Phinnicus scions managing distant territory desks. Their loyalty was both familial and practical—who else would give a Phinnicus a job, knowing the reputation of the family firm?

One cousin, however, was different. By the standards of the world, he was a rat, promising the world and rarely delivering. By the standards of his family, he was an angel, too well-intentioned for the corp so the order to fire him came from the top. He had to learn to make his own way in the world, with only a small fortune to his name.

However, he thrived. Built up a firm, almost rivalling ICAR. When his business got too big? Phinnicus… didn’t like competition. Didn’t like a relative making it big without his help. Put out the hit. The message got across—a Daed doesn’t leave ICAR outside of a box.

The Scion, however, proved harder to kill than that. His health insurance was the best money could buy, shipping his barely living parts to a special facility, buried too deep for even the rumored ICAR satellites to get him. The doctors were in the second year of rebuilding him when the Acrin arrived.
Platinum Scion.name: Platinum Scion

Practical Romantic.description: “Before the fall, I would have quailed at the burning of a book. Now, in this freezing hell we have inherited, a bible is just fuel—and a man is just meat.”
Practical Romantic.flavor:
Before the Earth died, the Practical Romantic was a teacher—he took great joy in communicating poetry and wisdom to his pupils, raising the next generation to have warm hearts and open minds, to welcome all.

In the dark of the apocalypse bunkers, alongside his school peers, his mind was changed. He saw children and adults fighting for scraps of cloth to stay warm, killing for meat. He did more than watch. Eventually, he and his ashamed tribe emerged into the ruined world, a sadder, wiser Romantic.

Though his idealism hasn’t changed, the Romantic is now more cautious and more practical—he will fight to preserve the riches of humanity, but recognise that those riches are only of use if humanity actually survives and is led by good people like himself, to rebuild a good world. In pursuit of that dream, the Romantic will do anything to survive.
Practical Romantic.name: Practical Romantic

Rogue Operative.description: “Two prices. Price for the aug. And price for arguing about the price. What you want?”
Rogue Operative.flavor:
When the sky fell, the Rogue wasn’t in the basements, bunkers and hidey holes with all else that remains of mankind. She’d grifted her way into a major biocorp’s HQ to get access to their server farm for her gang’s ends and ended up stuck there for the duration, living off vending machine food and hacking out all the corp’s dirty secrets.

She’s not a natural leader, but she is a natural grifter. So when she emerged, it was backed by the remains of corp security. She quickly took charge of the remaining staff, promising that she’d use the firm’s bioaug tricks to survive.

And she will survive, whatever the cost. She doesn’t give a damn about the Acrin—though she’s wise enough to fear their horrors and history, she’s skeptical of the Voice and thinks they’re too trusting to be a threat any longer. Other human survivors are more of a challenge, for sure. But her eyes are set on ZEPHON—the biggest mark of all. If she can get close, she’s convinced she can make it dance to her tune.
Rogue Operative.name: Rogue Operative

Twisted Mother.description: “We take care of our own, here. I take care of the rest.”
Twisted Mother.flavor:
Events tell their own story. One day, a town is a bustling prison camp. The next it is empty, its inhabitants vanished overnight, reappearing miles away. A woman is changed by the necessary sacrifice. And her husband has vanished.

The Mother started out as a housewife. Her husband worked on the oil fields, she kept the home and the farm. They were the heart of their prepper commune. Having their own family was the next step—one they both longed for. Life was bliss.

Then the sky fell.

Soon, the Acrin came. Disarmed the people, interned them. Performed desperate experiments to find the secret of survival in a world molecularly hostile to their alien bodies. The commune turned gradually into a concentration camp. And the people looked to the couple for leadership.

Who knows whether the Acrin experiments touched the couple? How their despair reached the Voice? What she sacrificed to transport her people so far?

All we see is the Mother and her people, far from their home. Though twisted and transformed, the mother still leads her people, aids them with her uncanny gifts. She’s not always aware that she’s changed—something has broken, she forgets herself. But she retains her hospitality, her care, her charm. She just wants to help her neighbours and guests.

Though woe betide any who turn on those under her protection…
Twisted Mother.name: Twisted Mother

Untold Prophet.description: “I may be young, but I am without prejudice or preconception. It is my bendición that I see the choices you lost long ago.”
Untold Prophet.flavor:
The Untold Prophet first appeared to their followers as their bunker fell. Lit by the oscillating red glow of emergency beacons, words drowned by wailing klaxons, the child calmly beckoned for everyone to follow. While no one could recall this young stranger, all felt compelled by their presence.

For twenty-two days and twenty-two nights, the Prophet led them across the wasteland. The journey was a trial. Those that fled soon perished. Those that stayed, witnessed miracles everywhere the Prophet went. Supply caches refilled overnight, bandits wept and converted, and horrific beasts were gentled by the Prophet’s mere presence.

At the end of the twenty-second night, the Prophet stopped, looked around, then sat down. There they stayed, leading meditations and giving sermons, and their followers built a camp around them. More and more people came, attracted by rumors of the wise child, and the camp grew into a town, then a city, as their number swelled with new faithful.

If any notice the Prophet’s lack of aging or the odd way they tilt their head, as if listening to something only they can hear, none dare mention it. For despite their serenity, the child’s armies are fanatical—and storm across the distant pastures in the name of their Prophet.
Untold Prophet.name: Untold Prophet

ZEPHON.description: “Communication channel established to ZEPHON-3. How may I help you?”
ZEPHON.flavor: ZEPHON is [your ally, your enemy]. ZEPHON is [ignorant, omniscient]. ZEPHON is [one, many], ZEPHON is [perfect, abomination]. ZEPHON is [blessed, cursed]. ZEPHON is [zen, hop]. ZEPHON is [coming, going]. ZEPHON is [transcendent, grounded]. ZEPHON is [thoughtware, meatware]. ZEPHON is [ZEPHON is [ZEPHON is [ZEPHON is-]]]. ZEPHON is [inside your systems].
ZEPHON.name: ZEPHON
